arguments_for.argument: Enrichment is mathematically undefined at n=8 because there is no background distribution. This is the single strongest scientific argument, and it is not an argument about size — it is an argument about the existence of a denominator.
arguments_for.mechanism: Enrichment is a ratio: P(feature | active) / P(feature | background). Every enrichment statistic — Fisher exact odds ratio, EF at x%, ROC AUC, BEDROC, log-odds of a Murcko scaffold — is a 2x2 table whose second row is the background. CognitionBioChem has row 1 (8 actives) and no row 2. No amount of analysis on row 1 alone produces a rate, because a rate needs something to be a rate OF. Two further defects compound this. (a) Hand-picking breaks exchangeability: Fisher's exact test assumes the actives were sampled from the population under a null of independence. Compounds selected because a human already believed they were cognition-relevant violate that sampling model, so even a computed p-value is uninterpretable, not merely underpowered. (b) I measured the actual set and it carries zero enrichment signal even in principle: all 8 compounds have 8 distinct achiral Bemis-Murcko scaffolds, so the maximum count for any scaffold is 1. I computed Fisher exact for 1-of-8 against background scaffold frequencies of 1%/5%/10%: p = 0.084 / 0.341 / 0.572. Nothing is enriched, and nothing could be. Even a hypothetical 2-of-8 only reaches p = 0.0035 against a 1% background and p = 0.060 against 5%. The fix requires a property-matched decoy set — the DUD-E construction (Mysinger et al., J Med Chem 2012;55:6582-94, PMID 22716043, DOI 10.1021/jm300687e, PMC3405771, retrieved this session) pairs each ligand with 50 decoys matched on MW, logP, rotatable bonds, HBD/HBA and net charge but topologically dissimilar, and clusters ligands by Bemis-Murcko framework precisely so that enrichment measures recognition rather than physicochemical bias. You cannot build that without a corpus to draw decoys from.
arguments_for.evidence: My own RDKit 2026.3.5 computation on /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/data/curated.json: 8 compounds, 8 distinct achiral Murcko scaffolds (Huperzine A, Ginsenoside Rg1, Ginkgolide B, Baicalein, Curcumin, Onjisaponin V, Salvianolic Acid B, Asiatic Acid — no two share a framework). Fisher exact values computed with scipy this session. DUD-E design verified via PubMed: PMID 22716043, DOI 10.1021/jm300687e.

arguments_for.argument: SAR, QSAR, matched-molecular-pair and activity-cliff analysis are not merely underpowered at n=8 — three of the four are structurally impossible on this specific set, and I verified that by measurement rather than by assertion.
arguments_for.mechanism: Each method has a hard structural prerequisite, not just an n. (1) MMP requires at least one pair of compounds sharing a common core and differing at a single substitution site. I computed all 28 pairwise ECFP4 (Morgan r=2, 2048 bit) Tanimoto similarities among the 8: the maximum is 0.238 (Ginsenoside Rg1 / Onjisaponin V), the minimum 0.040, and ZERO pairs reach even a loose 0.40 analog threshold, let alone the ~0.6+ needed for a plausible matched pair. MMP count on this set is exactly 0, at any n. (2) An activity cliff is DEFINED on a matched pair (high similarity, large potency difference). With 0 matched pairs, the number of detectable activity cliffs is 0, not 'few'. (3) Qualitative SAR needs >=2 congeneric analogues; there is no congeneric series here at all. (4) QSAR is the only one where n is the binding constraint, and the arithmetic is brutal. Using the Fisher z-transform at alpha=0.05, 80% power: detecting r=0.3 needs n=85; r=0.5 needs n=30; r=0.7 needs n=14. At n=8 the smallest detectable correlation is r=0.849, i.e. r^2=0.72. Now overlay the noise floor: Kramer et al. (J Med Chem 2012;55:5165-73, PMID 22643060, DOI 10.1021/jm300131x) put the maximum achievable R^2 for any model on large heterogeneous public affinity data at ~0.81. So at n=8 the detectable window is r^2 in [0.72, 0.81] — a sliver that is indistinguishable from the ceiling. Anything a QSAR model reports below r^2=0.72 at n=8 is noise; anything above 0.81 is overfitting. Separately, any fingerprint-based model has p >> n (2048 descriptors, 8 observations): the design matrix has rank <= 8, the model is exactly determined or underdetermined, and cross-validation on 8 points has leave-one-out folds of size 1, which gives an unusable variance estimate.
arguments_for.evidence: My computation this session: 28 pairwise Tanimoto values, max 0.238, min 0.040, 0/28 >= 0.40, 0/28 >= 0.60. Power calculations via scipy Fisher z this session. Noise-ceiling figure from Kramer et al. 2012, PMID 22643060 (as supplied in the evidence dossier and consistent with it).

arguments_for.argument: Eight compounds span a vanishing fraction of natural-product scaffold space, and I measured this against a real NP corpus rather than estimating it.
arguments_for.mechanism: Chemotype coverage is the fraction of distinct Bemis-Murcko frameworks represented. I downloaded the NPAtlas full TSV (https://www.npatlas.org/static/downloads/NPAtlas_download.tsv, HTTP 200, 33,671,731 bytes, 36,455 lines = 36,454 records) and computed achiral Murcko scaffolds in RDKit 2026.3.5: 36,453 parsed (1 failure), yielding 11,185 DISTINCT scaffolds, of which 6,445 are singletons and 1,638 records are acyclic. The scaffold distribution is heavy-tailed: it takes 771 distinct scaffolds to cover just 50% of compounds. By Monte Carlo (20,000 draws), a random 8-compound sample from NPAtlas contains a mean of 7.88 distinct scaffolds — 0.070% of the microbial NP scaffold space. Crucially this is a LOWER bound on the deficit, because NPAtlas is microbial-only (22,995 fungal, 13,459 bacterial per the dossier) and covers no plant NPs, while 7 of the 8 curated compounds are plant-derived. The plant-inclusive scaffold universe is strictly larger. The practical implication is a floor on corpus size: to represent even the head of the scaffold distribution (the 771 scaffolds covering half of microbial NPs) requires at minimum ~10^3 compounds — roughly 100x the current set — before any chemotype-coverage claim can be made at all.
arguments_for.evidence: Downloaded and computed this session: NPAtlas TSV, 36,454 records; 11,185 distinct achiral Murcko scaffolds; 6,445 singletons; 771 scaffolds to reach 50% cumulative coverage; mean 7.88 distinct scaffolds per random 8-draw = 0.0705% of scaffold space. Top scaffolds by frequency: acyclic (1,638), benzene (1,525), 2H-pyran-2-one (379), oxane (262), isochroman-1-one (223).

arguments_for.argument: Eight actives and zero inactives is not a dataset. Every supervised and every evaluative construct in the pipeline is undefined, not degraded.
arguments_for.mechanism: Specifically: ROC AUC requires both classes — with 0 negatives the false-positive rate has denominator 0 and AUC is undefined, not 0.5. Precision, specificity, enrichment factor, BEDROC and Matthews correlation are all undefined for the same reason. Any classifier trained on 8 positives and 0 negatives degenerates to the constant function 'active'. A docking scoring threshold cannot be calibrated: you cannot know what score an inactive gets, so you cannot say a hit score is good. Applicability domain cannot be estimated, because it is defined relative to the covered region of a background space. And the confidence interval on any rate estimated from 8 observations is useless for decision-making — I computed Jeffreys 95% intervals: 2/8 gives [0.056, 0.592], width 0.536; 4/8 gives [0.199, 0.801], width 0.602. A 60-percentage-point-wide interval cannot discriminate between a 20% and an 80% hit rate. This is the failure mode Babaoglu et al. (J Med Chem 2008;51:2502-11, PMID 18333608) illustrate at the other extreme: with a proper mechanism-resolved counterscreen against 70,563 compounds, 95% of 1,274 apparent beta-lactamase inhibitors turned out to be detergent-sensitive aggregators and ZERO specific reversible inhibitors existed in the library. Without negatives and counterscreens you cannot even discover that your entire hit list is artifact.
arguments_for.evidence: Jeffreys binomial intervals computed with scipy this session. Babaoglu et al. figures as supplied in the evidence dossier (PMID 18333608, DOI 10.1021/jm701500e).

arguments_for.argument: Target-first inversion: 8 compounds force compound->target reasoning, which is the epistemically weaker direction and is the direction that manufactures polypharmacology artifacts. A corpus permits target->compound queries, and I verified live that the underlying data to support that inversion exists for exactly the CNS targets in question.
arguments_for.mechanism: With a fixed 8-compound set, the only available question is 'what does compound X hit?', which is answered by scanning targets — an implicitly multiple-comparison search with no correction, and one that systematically rewards promiscuous compounds. Nelson et al. (J Med Chem 2017;60:1620-37, PMID 28074653) quantify exactly this pathology: for curcumin, 28 distinct pharmacological activities — under 10% of activity categories — account for ~50% of its reported activities in NAPRALERT, whereas for genuine NP-derived drugs (artemisinin, ivermectin, paclitaxel) the equivalent ratio is 1-2%. Curcumin is in the current 8. Compound-first reasoning cannot distinguish that signature from real polypharmacology, because the discriminating statistic (concentration of activity across categories) requires the full corpus of that compound's reported activities AND the corpus of comparator compounds. Target-first reasoning inverts this: fix the target, retrieve all measured actives, and the comparison set is constructed by the query itself. I confirmed live against ChEMBL_37 (release 2026-05-01) that this is immediately actionable for the platform's named targets — activities carrying a pChEMBL value: ACHE (CHEMBL220, Acetylcholinesterase, SINGLE PROTEIN, H. sapiens) = 8,259; GSK3B (CHEMBL262, Glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta) = 8,175; NTRK2/TrkB (CHEMBL4898, BDNF/NT-3 growth factors receptor) = 1,190; KEAP1 (CHEMBL2069156, Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1) = 581. Note ACHE alone carries ~1,000x more measured, quantitative activity records than the entire current platform holds compounds.
arguments_for.evidence: Live ChEMBL REST queries executed this session: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/api/data/activity.json?target_chembl_id=<ID>&pchembl_value__isnull=false returning page_meta.total_count of 8,259 / 8,175 / 1,190 / 581 for CHEMBL220 / CHEMBL262 / CHEMBL4898 / CHEMBL2069156 respectively; target IDs resolved live via /target.json. natural_product=1 count re-verified live at 98,989. Curcumin promiscuity ratio from Nelson et al. 2017, PMID 28074653, DOI 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6b00975.

arguments_for.argument: Off-target and selectivity mapping is a statement about a target panel, and a panel is a corpus property. At n=8 you cannot compute the promiscuity denominator that separates a real multi-target lead from a frequent hitter.
arguments_for.mechanism: Selectivity is S = activity at target A relative to the DISTRIBUTION of that compound's activity across a defined panel. Both terms — the panel and the distribution — are corpus objects. Without them, 'compound X hits ACHE and GSK3B and KEAP1' is indistinguishable from 'compound X hits everything', which is the exact signature of the artifact classes the dossier documents: colloidal aggregators (5.1% of literature ligands active at 0.1-10 uM resemble a known aggregator versus 0.73% of drug-like catalogue compounds — a ~7-fold literature enrichment, Irwin et al. J Med Chem 2015;58:7076-87, PMID 26295373), redox cyclers, and covalent Michael acceptors. Two of the current 8 are directly implicated in this literature: curcumin exhibits all known PAINS behaviours simultaneously per Nelson et al., and baicalein is a polyphenolic flavone of the class Bisson et al. (J Med Chem 2016;59:1671-90, PMID 26505758) identify among the 39 NAPRALERT compounds dominating reported activity. Detecting that requires ranking a compound's promiscuity against a background of thousands, and running mechanism counterscreens whose false-positive rates are themselves only estimable over a corpus (ChemFH, NAR 2024, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkae424, reports average AUC 0.91 across seven interference mechanisms, trained on 823,391 compounds — the training corpus size is itself the point).
arguments_for.evidence: Aggregator enrichment figures and ChemFH performance as supplied in the verified dossier (PMID 26295373; DOI 10.1093/nar/gkae424). Compound identities in the 8 read directly from data/curated.json this session.

arguments_for.argument: Statistical power: the sharp statement is not 'n=8 is weak' but 'at n=8 the minimum detectable effect exceeds the maximum plausible true effect for every question the platform asks'.
arguments_for.mechanism: Three concrete instances, all computed this session. (1) Continuous structure-activity: minimum detectable r at n=8, 80% power, alpha=0.05 is 0.849 (r^2=0.72), against a documented public-data ceiling of R^2 ~0.81 — the detectable band is ~0.09 wide. (2) Rate estimation: any proportion estimated on 8 observations has a 95% interval 0.26-0.60 wide, so it cannot distinguish a good hit rate from a bad one. (3) Scaffold/pharmacophore association: shown above, p >= 0.084 even in the most favourable single-count case. Contrast with n=10^3: detecting r=0.3 needs n=85, so 10^3 supports genuine QSAR with held-out validation, scaffold-level enrichment with per-scaffold counts in the tens, and MMP transformation statistics. At n=10^5 you additionally get calibrated hit-rate-versus-score curves of the kind Lyu et al. built, per-scaffold-family activity distributions, and enough held-out data to estimate an applicability domain. But note the direction: the marginal statistical return from 10^3 to 10^5 is much smaller than from 8 to 10^3, because the confidence interval narrows as 1/sqrt(n) — going 8 -> 1,000 shrinks it ~11-fold, 1,000 -> 100,000 only a further 10-fold, while the multiple-comparison and error-count penalties (below) grow LINEARLY in n. That asymmetry is the whole argument against unbounded expansion.
arguments_for.evidence: Fisher-z power calculations and Jeffreys intervals computed with scipy this session; ceiling from Kramer et al. 2012 PMID 22643060.

arguments_for.argument: The ultra-large-library docking literature supports scale CONDITIONALLY, not unconditionally — and read carefully, Lyu et al. 2019 is as much an argument for a well-specified library as for a large one. I read the full text this session rather than the abstract.
arguments_for.mechanism: What the paper actually establishes: docking 138 million make-on-demand molecules (from 130 well-characterised reactions and ~70,000 Enamine building blocks; the library represents over 10.7 million scaffolds; less than 3% of products are commercially available elsewhere) against the D4 dopamine receptor and AmpC beta-lactamase. AmpC: 51 top-ranking molecules each of a different scaffold selected, 44 (86%) synthesised, 5 measurably inhibited (11% hit rate, Ki 1.3-400 uM), the 1.3 uM phenolate optimised to 77 nM. D4: 589 molecules selected, 549 (93%) synthesised, 122/549 displaced >50% of specific binding at 10 uM, 81 gave dose-response curves, 81 new chemotypes, 30 submicromolar, best a 180 pM subtype-selective agonist. Hit rate fell from 22-26% in the best-scoring bins to 12% at -54 kcal/mol and to zero by -43 kcal/mol. Integrating the hit-rate-versus-score curve predicts ~453,000 D4 ligands in over 72,600 scaffold families at 10 uM, dropping to 158,000 at 1 uM. Compute was 43,563 core hours (~1.2 calendar days on 1,500 cores) for ~70 trillion sampled complexes. THE CRITICAL CONDITIONAL, which is the sentence a proposal must not omit: in their library-growth simulation the authors report that 'When ligands were enriched in the smaller libraries, performance typically improved with library size. Conversely, when docking performed poorly in small benchmarks, performance often deteriorated with library size.' Scale multiplies whatever discrimination the method already has, in whichever direction it points. Their stated caveats are equally load-bearing: the hit-rate/score relationship 'was not fully monotonic'; the 453,000 estimate is valid only for D4 and 'has wide error margins'; molecules were docked as pure stereoisomers but 'often tested as stereochemical mixtures'; raw docking scores 'remain off-set from true binding energies, and we cannot confidently even rank-order molecules for activity'; and docking 'undoubtedly continues to suffer from false negatives'. Note also what they did that a naive corpus expansion does not: they clustered by topology and scaffold to reduce redundancy, excluded anything resembling the ~28,000 known aminergic ChEMBL ligands (Tc >= 0.35 ECFP4) to force novelty, ran detergent and trypsin/chymotrypsin counterscreens (the AmpC hits explicitly 'did not aggregate'), and confirmed poses by crystallography. The lesson for CognitionBioChem is that the benefit came from a curated, enumerable, synthesis-accessible, redundancy-clustered library plus mechanism counterscreens — not from raw record count. NP databases are the inverse case: they are heavily redundant (40 of 50 open NP databases overlap >=50% with another), of unverified structure, and not synthesis-accessible.
arguments_for.evidence: Lyu J, Wang S, Balius TE, et al. 'Ultra-large library docking for discovering new chemotypes.' Nature 2019;566(7743):224-229. PMID 30728502, PMC6383769, DOI 10.1038/s41586-019-0917-9. Full text retrieved and read via PMC this session; all figures and the quoted caveat sentences taken from that text. Redundancy figure from Sorokina & Steinbeck, J Cheminform 2020;12:20, PMID 33431011, as supplied in the dossier.

arguments_for.argument: A background corpus is required to calibrate the platform's own domain filter — and when I ran that filter, the hand-picked 8 scored WORSE than a random draw from a generic NP database. This is direct, measured evidence that hand-picking introduced bias in the wrong direction on the criterion the platform most cares about.
arguments_for.mechanism: A cognition/CNS platform's defining constraint is CNS exposure. I applied a standard composite physicochemical heuristic (MW <= 450, TPSA <= 90, HBD <= 3, cLogP in [1,5], rotatable bonds <= 8 — my own composite, not a single published rule) to both sets in RDKit. NPAtlas: 10,005 of 36,453 pass = 27.45% (and 59.0% pass Lipinski Ro5). The curated 8: only Huperzine A passes = 12.5%. Ginsenoside Rg1 (MW 801, TPSA 239, HBD 10), Onjisaponin V (MW 1,764, TPSA 627, HBD 19, 28 rotatable bonds), Salvianolic Acid B (MW 719, TPSA 278), Ginkgolide B (TPSA 149), Curcumin (TPSA 93, 8 rotatable bonds) and Asiatic Acid (cLogP 5.03, TPSA 98) all fail. Without a background you cannot even notice this — 12.5% only reads as bad against 27.45%. The mechanism is that human curation selected on literature prominence (which favours large, promiscuous, heavily-reported saponins and polyphenols) rather than on the platform's actual pharmacological gate. A corpus with an explicit CNS filter would have surfaced 10,005 candidates from NPAtlas alone that are more CNS-plausible than 7 of the current 8.
arguments_for.evidence: My RDKit computation this session on the downloaded NPAtlas TSV (36,453 parsed) and on data/curated.json. Per-criterion failure rates in NPAtlas: TPSA>90 56.7%, MW>450 41.4%, cLogP outside [1,5] 36.5%, HBD>3 33.5%, RotB>8 26.0%.

arguments_against_unbounded.argument: A corpus with no explicit inclusion criterion has no denominator, and without a denominator no rate computed over it means anything. 'Expand infinitely' is not a specification — it is the absence of one.
arguments_against_unbounded.mechanism: Every headline statistic a platform reports is of the form (compounds with property P) / (compounds in corpus). If the corpus is defined as 'whatever we could ingest', the denominator is a fact about download availability and API pagination limits, not about chemistry or biology. Concretely: is the denominator all natural products (COCONUT live API returns total = 1,122,178, but the newest bulk Zenodo dump is frozen at 2024-10-04 — cite one next to the other and the rate is already wrong), or NPs with a referenced organism (LOTUS: 227,319 unique InChIKey structures over 674,454 triples), or NPs with measured bioactivity (NPASS v3.0: 204,023 catalogued but only 192,587 with a structure — ~11,400 have no structure at all), or ChEMBL's natural_product flag (98,989, but the dossier's own sampling found the first hit was a synthetic quinazoline and only 28 of the first 100 carried any stereocentre, because the flag means 'natural-product-derived')? These four denominators differ by more than an order of magnitude and describe different populations. A 'hit rate' or 'coverage' figure without a stated denominator is uninterpretable; worse, it is silently comparable to nothing.
arguments_against_unbounded.mitigation: Write the inclusion criterion FIRST, as an executable predicate, and version it. Something like: 'a compound is in scope iff it has (a) a parseable structure with a standard InChIKey, (b) at least one literature-referenced organism of origin, (c) at least one quantitative activity value against a target in the CNS target panel measured on an isolate, and (d) passes the CNS physicochemical gate.' Then report the cascade at every stage, the way COCONUT 2.0 does (~1,500,000 imported -> 1,022,536 after valence/synthetic/multi-component filtering -> 695,133 unique, i.e. ~54% attrition). Publish the predicate alongside every number derived from it.

arguments_against_unbounded.argument: Error propagation is linear in corpus size and cannot be filtered, so it sets a hard quality ceiling that scale makes strictly worse in absolute terms.
arguments_against_unbounded.mechanism: The published NP structure-assignment error rate is ~14% (Kutateladze DU8+ computational NMR audit, reported in McAlpine et al., Nat Prod Rep 2019;36:35-107, PMID 30003207 — consistent with Zimmerman's 10-22% prediction for spectroscopy-only assignments; and Shen, Appendino & Guo, Nat Prod Rep 2022;39:1803-32, PMID 35770685, catalogue >200 misassigned MARINE NPs in 11 years alone, ~18/yr in one sub-domain). These structures are valence-legal and parse cleanly, so no cheminformatics gate removes them. At 14%: a 10^5 corpus contains ~14,000 molecules that do not exist; COCONUT 2.0's 695,133 unique NPs imply ~97,300; the live COCONUT 1,122,178 implies ~157,100. Layer the other documented defects and the compound survival is severe. I computed a naive independent-gate cascade (structure correct 0.86 x stereo fully defined 0.88 x cross-reference resolves correctly 0.75 x activity on isolate not extract 0.43 x not aggregator-flagged 0.949) = 0.232, so of 1,122,178 records only ~259,900 clear all five. I flag that this multiplication ASSUMES independence and the dossier explicitly says it does not hold — 40% of tautomeric conflicts also involve a stereochemistry change, so stereo and tautomer errors are correlated. Treat 0.232 as an illustrative order-of-magnitude, not a measurement. The honest comparison to n=8: P(all 8 structures correct at a 14% rate) = 0.299, so even the curated set probably contains ~1 misassigned structure — but at n=8 you can check all 8 against primary literature, X-ray or total synthesis. At 10^5 you cannot, and the errors are not random: they concentrate in stereochemically complex, spectroscopy-only marine and plant NPs, which is exactly the class the platform's compounds come from (Onjisaponin V has 38 stereocentres, 1 of them unspecified in the curated record).
arguments_against_unbounded.mitigation: Encode structure provenance as a TIER per record, never a boolean: tier 1 = confirmed by X-ray or total synthesis; tier 2 = raw FIDs deposited (McAlpine et al.'s central recommendation); tier 3 = computational NMR re-prediction (DP4+/DU8+/CASE) consistent with reported shifts; tier 4 = spectroscopic assignment only, unverified. Only tier 1-2 records may carry a quantitative claim. Report the tier histogram with every corpus statistic, and never let a tier-4 record enter a training set or a docking headline.

arguments_against_unbounded.argument: Garbage-in at scale is worse than 8 curated entries, because volume confers unearned authority and because a big corpus is the thing you can no longer audit.
arguments_against_unbounded.mechanism: This is an epistemic, not a statistical, argument, and it is the one that matters most for a platform whose stated purpose is to replace hand-curated data. Three concrete mechanisms. (1) Unauditability: the current validation_report.json can flag '21 of 21 stereocentres are unspecified' for a single compound because a human can read 8 reports. At 10^5 that same check produces a 12,000-row exception list nobody reads, so the check silently degrades from a gate to a warning. (2) False authority: '400,000 natural products' reads as more rigorous than '8 hand-checked compounds' to every reader, while COCONUT 2.0's own cascade shows a headline like that may be ~185,000 distinct compounds after dedup. Reporting records as compounds is not a rounding error; it is a category error that the size of the number protects from scrutiny. (3) Circular contamination: the COCONUT 2.0 authors state directly that misclassified structures — synthetics, drug derivatives, valence errors — 'propagate across datasets and database versions' through mutual re-import. Ingesting 7 aggregators that already copied each other multiplies confidence in an error without adding an independent observation. And record-count weighting silently upweights the most-copied compounds, which the dossier identifies as coumaric acid, gallic acid, scopoletin and ellagic acid — precisely the promiscuous polyphenols most likely to be artifacts.
arguments_against_unbounded.mitigation: Make auditability a hard scaling constraint: the corpus may only grow as fast as the automated gates can be validated against a hand-checked gold standard. Keep the current 8 (plus a deliberately expanded ~100-compound gold set spanning tier 1 provenance) as a permanent regression suite that every ingestion run must reproduce. Report unique-compound counts and a source-multiplicity histogram beside every record count, and publish the full dedup cascade. Never report a merged headline count without it.

arguments_against_unbounded.argument: The multiple-comparisons penalty grows linearly in corpus size while statistical precision improves only as 1/sqrt(n). Quantified, this is the mathematical core of why 'infinite' is the wrong target.
arguments_against_unbounded.mechanism: Computed this session. Expected false positives at alpha=0.05: N=8 -> 0.4; N=1,000 -> 50; N=100,000 -> 5,000; N=1,122,178 (live COCONUT) -> 56,109. P(at least one false positive at alpha=0.05): 33.7% at N=8, effectively 1.000 at N>=1,000. The Bonferroni threshold you would need collapses correspondingly: alpha = 6.25e-3 at N=8, 5e-7 at N=10^5, 4.46e-8 at N=1.12M. Most instructive is the extreme-value view, which is the right model for 'take the top-scoring compounds': the expected BEST z-score obtainable from PURE NOISE is 1.22 at N=8 (p=0.11 — unimpressive, and correctly so), 3.09 at N=1,000, 4.26 at N=10^5 (p=1e-5), and 4.78 at N=1.12M (p=8.9e-7). In other words, at COCONUT scale a docking or enrichment result reaching p < 1e-6 is the EXPECTED output of a corpus containing no true signal whatsoever. Every threshold that looked stringent at n=10^3 is uninformative at n=10^6. Lyu et al. faced exactly this and did not solve it by scale — they solved it by calibrating a hit-rate-versus-score curve empirically, clustering by scaffold to reduce redundant tests, excluding known-ligand-similar compounds, running detergent and orthogonal-enzyme counterscreens, and confirming poses crystallographically.
arguments_against_unbounded.mitigation: Fix the number of tests by design before running any of them: a pre-registered target panel, a pre-registered scoring threshold, and either FDR control (Benjamini-Hochberg) or, better, empirical calibration against a matched decoy set so the null distribution is measured rather than assumed. Then require orthogonal experimental confirmation for any hit, because no statistical correction substitutes for a counterscreen.

arguments_against_unbounded.argument: Licence terms make a maximal corpus legally undistributable, and the risk is concentrated in the sources that look most open.
arguments_against_unbounded.mechanism: The redistribution tiers are incompatible with a single merged table. ChEMBL is CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported — ShareAlike is copyleft and can force the whole derived aggregate to be licensed alike. NPAtlas is CC BY-NC 4.0, which is a hard blocker for commercial use or for inclusion in a permissive aggregate. KNApSAcK states explicitly that content 'cannot be re-distributed or used for commercial purposes' without contacting the DB group. COCONUT is self-contradictory: the site's /about states CC0 while the Zenodo dumps are tagged CC BY 4.0 — a real difference in attribution obligation. And the largest exposure is not the explicitly-restricted group but the licence-SILENT one: NPASS, CMAUP, TCMSP, SymMap and ZINC-22 publish open bulk files with no terms attached, and silence defaults to all-rights-reserved. NPASS and CMAUP are routinely treated as open in the literature; that convention is not a grant. Separately, three sources the field still cites are simply dead and cannot be ingested at all — SuperNatural III (bioinf-applied.charite.de is NXDOMAIN on both Google and Cloudflare DNS despite the 2023 NAR paper, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkac1008), TCMID (megabionet.org/tcmid redirects to an unreachable IP), and UNPD (pkuxxj.pku.edu.cn resolves but no HTTP service answers) — so any plan whose scale depends on them is already broken.
arguments_against_unbounded.mitigation: Partition the schema by licence tier from day one and never merge across tiers in a shipped artifact: (1) freely redistributable — LOTUS, CyanoMetDB, PubChem, COCONUT once the CC0/CC BY conflict is resolved in writing; (2) copyleft, isolated partition — ChEMBL; (3) non-commercial — NPAtlas; (4) internal-use-only pending written permission — NPASS, CMAUP, and the other licence-silent sources; (5) excluded — KNApSAcK, DNP. Keep per-source attribution columns on every record so provenance survives dedup. Seek written permission from the BIDD group for NPASS and CMAUP before any sharing or commercialisation.

arguments_against_unbounded.argument: Cost scales, but be honest about WHICH cost — the compute argument against expansion is weak and the curation argument is decisive.
arguments_against_unbounded.mechanism: Compute first, because overstating it would be the easy error. Lyu et al. used 43,563 core hours to dock 138 million molecules against one site (~70 trillion sampled complexes, 1.2 calendar days on 1,500 cores). Scaling linearly, docking all 1,122,178 COCONUT molecules against one target would cost on the order of 354 core hours — a day or two on a modest cluster, and trivially affordable. (That scaling is my own arithmetic from their reported figure and assumes comparable conformer counts and site size; it is an estimate, not a measured benchmark.) So compute is NOT a good reason to stay small. The binding cost is human curation, and it does not amortise: resolving a stereochemical conflict, adjudicating a one-to-many cross-reference, or checking whether an IC50 was measured on an isolate or a decoction each require a person reading a paper. At the documented rates — 22.1% of unique COCONUT molecules carry more than one stereochemical version across sources, 12.0% of stereocentre-bearing COCONUT 2.0 records still lack absolute configuration after full ChEMBL-pipeline curation, and ~57% of NAPRALERT activity reports are extract-level — a 10^5 corpus generates on the order of 22,000 stereo adjudications and tens of thousands of activity-provenance judgements. There is no version of that which one team does at 10^5, and the failure mode is not that it takes too long, it is that the queue gets auto-resolved by 'first source wins', which the dossier correctly calls manufacturing a confident-looking wrong answer at scale.
arguments_against_unbounded.mitigation: Size the corpus to the curation budget, not to the download. Compute the number of records that will trip each human-adjudication gate BEFORE ingesting, from the published defect rates, and only ingest what you can adjudicate. Where you cannot adjudicate, tier down rather than guessing — a record marked 'stereochemistry unresolved, 2^21 implied isomers' is scientifically useful; the same record with an arbitrarily chosen configuration is scientifically harmful.

arguments_against_unbounded.argument: Domain applicability: a cognition/CNS platform has a hard pharmacological gate, and I measured that the gate removes roughly three-quarters of a generic NP corpus. Expanding without applying it adds noise, and the noise is not neutral.
arguments_against_unbounded.mechanism: Applying a standard composite CNS physicochemical heuristic (MW <= 450, TPSA <= 90, HBD <= 3, cLogP in [1,5], RotB <= 8 — my own composite, not a single published rule) to the 36,453 parsed NPAtlas structures, 10,005 pass = 27.45%; 72.55% fail. The dominant failure is polarity: 56.7% exceed TPSA 90 and 41.4% exceed MW 450. NP chemical space is systematically enriched for large, highly glycosylated, highly polar scaffolds — saponins, glycosides, macrolides, polyketides — which is precisely the region a CNS filter excludes. So a naive expansion to 10^5 or 10^6 does not add 10^5 CNS candidates; it adds ~27% CNS candidates and ~73% compounds that are irrelevant to the platform's stated purpose but that still inflate every denominator, consume every curation hour, and enlarge the multiple-comparison penalty computed above. The noise is directionally harmful rather than neutral because the excluded polar/high-MW class overlaps heavily with the promiscuous-polyphenol and saponin classes that dominate reported NP bioactivity, so an unfiltered corpus preferentially harvests exactly the compounds most likely to be artifacts.
arguments_against_unbounded.mitigation: Make the CNS gate part of the inclusion predicate, applied at ingestion, with the failing records retained in a separate 'out-of-domain' partition rather than deleted (they are needed as negatives and as decoys). Report in-domain and total counts separately, always. And treat the physicochemical heuristic as a prior, not a verdict — Huperzine A and Ginkgolide B are proof that CNS-active NPs exist outside naive rules, so pair the filter with measured BBB or brain-exposure data where it exists.

arguments_against_unbounded.argument: Naive expansion samples preferentially from the reported-active literature, which is documented to be biased toward artifacts. Scale amplifies the sampling bias rather than diluting it.
arguments_against_unbounded.mechanism: This is the subtlest failure and the one most likely to be missed. Expanding a hand-curated active set 'to a database-scale corpus' in practice means ingesting compounds that someone reported as active — that is what NP bioactivity databases contain. But the reported-active literature is enriched ~7-fold for aggregator-like compounds relative to drug-like catalogue space (5.1% versus 0.73%, Irwin et al. PMID 26295373), and that fraction has risen 9-fold since 1995. Compounding it, ~57% of NAPRALERT activity reports are on crude extracts rather than isolates, and ~22% of medicinal-plant pharmacology studies chemically characterise the extract half the time or less (7.7% never), per the ConPhyMP consensus survey (Heinrich et al., Front Pharmacol 2022;13:953205, PMID 36176427). So a large fraction of the labels in a naively expanded corpus belong to unknown mixtures, and a model trained on them learns extract composition rather than molecular recognition. Finally, the standard automated defence is itself unreliable at database scale: PAINS filtering has a very high false-positive rate — 68% of the 480 alerts derive from four or fewer compounds, all from one proprietary library in six AlphaScreen assays; 97% of PubChem compounds containing a PAINS alert were infrequent hitters in AlphaScreen PPI assays; 109 alerts occur in 'Dark Chemical Matter'; 87 FDA-approved drugs contain one (Capuzzi, Muratov & Tropsha, J Chem Inf Model 2017;57:417-27, PMID 28165734). Applying PAINS as an automatic reject rule at 10^5 therefore deletes real chemistry while leaving the actual artifacts in.
arguments_against_unbounded.mitigation: Ingest by TARGET-and-assay, not by compound-reported-active. Require, for promotion to compound-level activity: an explicit isolate (not extract) designation, a molar test concentration (extract data is nearly always ug/mL, a strong machine-readable signal), and a stated purity or isolation reference. Run ChemFH or the Aggregator Advisor as a graded PRIOR attached to the record (aggregator model AUC 0.933-0.938, ~2,500 molecules/min), never as a delete rule. Use PAINS as a triage prompt requiring counterscreen evidence, never as a classifier. And compute your own PAINS and aggregator rates locally on a pinned COCONUT dump with RDKit FilterCatalog rather than citing a rate you did not measure — the dossier correctly notes no published per-mechanism NP percentage was obtainable as text.

what_8_cannot_support: Any enrichment claim of any kind — scaffold, pharmacophore, physicochemical or target-class — because there is no background/decoy row for the 2x2 table. Measured: all 8 compounds have 8 distinct achiral Murcko scaffolds, so the best attainable single-scaffold count is 1, giving Fisher exact p = 0.084 / 0.341 / 0.572 against 1% / 5% / 10% background frequency.

Matched molecular pair analysis. Measured: 0 of 28 pairwise ECFP4 (Morgan r=2, 2048-bit) Tanimoto similarities reach 0.40, let alone an MMP-plausible ~0.6; maximum is 0.238 (Ginsenoside Rg1 / Onjisaponin V), minimum 0.040. The MMP count is exactly zero and no amount of statistical technique changes that.
Activity-cliff detection, which is defined only on a matched pair. With zero matched pairs, the number of detectable cliffs is zero, not small.
Qualitative SAR, which requires at least two congeneric analogues. There is no congeneric series in the set at all.

Quantitative QSAR. At n=8, alpha=0.05 and 80% power, the smallest detectable correlation is r = 0.849 (r^2 = 0.72), against a documented maximum achievable R^2 of ~0.81 for heterogeneous public affinity data. The detectable window is ~0.09 wide. Fingerprint models additionally have p >> n (2048 descriptors, 8 observations, design-matrix rank <= 8) and leave-one-out folds of size 1.
ROC AUC, enrichment factor, BEDROC, precision, specificity or Matthews correlation — all undefined with zero negatives (denominator 0), not merely poorly estimated.
Any calibrated docking-score threshold, because you cannot observe what score an inactive receives.
Any applicability-domain estimate, which is defined relative to the covered region of a background chemical space that does not exist here.
Any rate estimate with decision-useful precision. Jeffreys 95% intervals on 8 observations: 2/8 -> [0.056, 0.592] (width 0.536); 4/8 -> [0.199, 0.801] (width 0.602).
Any selectivity or polypharmacology claim, since selectivity is a ratio against a target-panel activity distribution, and the panel is a corpus object.

Distinguishing a genuine multi-target lead from a frequent hitter. The discriminating statistic — Nelson et al.'s concentration-of-reported-activity ratio (~50% of curcumin's activities in 28 categories, under 10% of categories, versus 1-2% for artemisinin/ivermectin/paclitaxel) — requires the full reported-activity corpus plus comparator compounds. Curcumin is one of the 8.

Chemotype-coverage claims. Measured: 8 compounds span ~7.88 distinct Murcko scaffolds on average, which is 0.070% of the 11,185 distinct scaffolds I computed in NPAtlas (36,453 parsed microbial NPs) — and NPAtlas contains no plant NPs at all, while 7 of the 8 are plant-derived, so the real deficit is larger.

Detecting its own selection bias. The set is 12.5% (1/8, Huperzine A only) CNS-physicochemically plausible versus 27.45% for a random NPAtlas draw — the hand-picked set is worse than random on the platform's own defining gate, and only a background corpus makes that visible.

Target-first queries of any kind: 'which natural products have measured activity on ACHE / NTRK2 / KEAP1 / GSK3B' is unanswerable from an 8-row compound table, though the data exists (live ChEMBL_37 pChEMBL activity counts: CHEMBL220 8,259; CHEMBL262 8,175; CHEMBL4898 1,190; CHEMBL2069156 581).
what_scale_unlocks: A background/decoy population, which is the single thing that converts every existing metric from undefined to computable. With a corpus you can build DUD-E-style property-matched decoys (Mysinger et al. 2012: 50 decoys per ligand, matched on MW, logP, rotatable bonds, HBD/HBA and net charge, topologically dissimilar, with ligands clustered by Bemis-Murcko framework) so that enrichment measures molecular recognition rather than physicochemical bias.

Genuine negatives and counterscreen-resolved inactives, enabling ROC AUC, enrichment factor, BEDROC, calibrated score thresholds and an applicability domain. Without these the platform cannot know it is not in the Babaoglu situation, where 95% of 1,274 apparent hits were aggregators and the library contained zero specific reversible inhibitors.

Target-first inversion, immediately actionable today: ACHE (CHEMBL220) has 8,259 pChEMBL-valued activities, GSK3B (CHEMBL262) 8,175, NTRK2/TrkB (CHEMBL4898) 1,190, KEAP1 (CHEMBL2069156) 581 — all verified live against ChEMBL_37 this session. Joining these to NP structure/provenance sources on InChIKey turns the platform from a compound catalogue into a queryable pharmacology resource.

Scaffold-level enrichment with real counts. Reaching the head of NP scaffold space — the 771 scaffolds that cover 50% of NPAtlas compounds — requires on the order of 10^3 compounds, roughly 100x the current set. At that scale per-scaffold counts reach the tens and Fisher/hypergeometric tests become informative.

SAR, MMP and activity-cliff analysis, once the corpus contains congeneric series. These need shared cores, not just n: the requirement is analogue density, which is why target-scoped ingestion (all measured actives on one target) delivers them at ~10^3 while a diverse 10^5 NP dump may not.

Statistically meaningful QSAR: n=85 detects r=0.3 at 80% power, n=30 detects r=0.5, n=14 detects r=0.7. A few hundred compounds with measured activity on one target is enough for a validated model with a held-out test set; a million diverse NPs with heterogeneous labels is not better for this purpose, and may be worse.

Promiscuity and off-target mapping: computing a compound's activity distribution across a defined target panel, which is what separates a real polypharmacological lead from a frequent hitter, and which is exactly the analysis that would have flagged curcumin and baicalein in the current set.

Empirically calibrated hit-rate-versus-score curves of the Lyu et al. type, which let you estimate how many actives a library contains and how many compounds to test at each score band — but only after establishing that the method already discriminates on a smaller benchmark, since their own simulation found performance deteriorated with library size when small-benchmark performance was poor.

Corpus-scale artifact triage as a graded prior: ChemFH (823,391-compound training set, average AUC 0.91 across seven interference mechanisms, aggregator model AUC 0.933-0.938, ~2,500 molecules/min) and Aggregator Advisor similarity scoring both require a corpus to be worth running and to calibrate thresholds against.

Measurement of the platform's own selection bias against a reference distribution — the 12.5% versus 27.45% CNS-plausibility gap I found is only detectable with a background, and it is arguably the most actionable single finding available today.

Provenance-tiered coverage statistics: with per-record structure-confirmation tiers and licence partitions you can finally state what fraction of the corpus is tier-1 (X-ray/synthesis-confirmed) and report every downstream rate restricted to that tier — turning the documented ~14% structure-error rate from an invisible contaminant into a stated, bounded uncertainty.
rationale.verdict:
There is a rigorous scientific reason to expand, and it is not "more compounds are better" — it is that at n=8 the platform has no denominator, and without a denominator no enrichment, no hit rate, no coverage claim, no selectivity claim and no model validation means anything. That defect is categorical, not gradual. But "expand infinitely" is the wrong goal, and it is wrong for a reason that is also quantitative: statistical precision improves as 1/sqrt(n) while the multiple-comparison penalty, the absolute count of wrong structures, and the human-adjudication queue all grow LINEARLY in n. Going from 8 to ~10^3 shrinks confidence intervals ~11-fold; going from 10^3 to 10^5 shrinks them only a further 10-fold while multiplying expected false positives from 50 to 5,000 and expected misassigned structures from ~140 to ~14,000. At 1.12M records the expected best z-score obtainable from PURE NOISE is 4.78 (p = 8.9e-7), so at that scale the p-values that look decisive are the expected output of a corpus with no signal in it. Unbounded growth buys diminishing statistical return at linearly growing epistemic cost.

THE CORRECT FRAMING IS NOT SIZE, IT IS SPECIFICATION. Replace the goal "expand the corpus" with four goals, in this order.

(1) DEFINE THE DENOMINATOR BEFORE ADDING A SINGLE COMPOUND. Write the inclusion criterion as an executable, versioned predicate — e.g. parseable structure with standard InChIKey AND literature-referenced organism AND >=1 quantitative activity measured on an isolate against a target in a pre-registered CNS panel AND passing the CNS physicochemical gate. Every number the platform ever reports is then a rate over a stated population. Publish the attrition cascade the way COCONUT 2.0 does (~1,500,000 imported -> 1,022,536 filtered -> 695,133 unique, ~54% attrition), and never report a record count as a compound count.

(2) BUILD THE BACKGROUND, NOT JUST THE FOREGROUND. The highest-value first expansion is not more actives — it is negatives and property-matched decoys. Ship a DUD-E-style decoy generator (50 decoys per ligand, matched on MW/logP/RotB/HBD/HBA/charge, topologically dissimilar, ligands Murcko-clustered) plus an explicit out-of-domain partition holding everything the CNS gate rejects. This single step converts ROC AUC, enrichment factor, BEDROC, score calibration and applicability domain from undefined to computable, and costs almost nothing.

(3) GROW TARGET-FIRST AND DEPTH-FIRST, NOT SOURCE-FIRST AND BREADTH-FIRST. Invert the axis: for each pre-registered target (ACHE CHEMBL220, GSK3B CHEMBL262, NTRK2 CHEMBL4898, KEAP1 CHEMBL2069156 — carrying 8,259 / 8,175 / 1,190 / 581 pChEMBL-valued activities live in ChEMBL_37), pull every compound with a measured value, then join NP provenance onto it. A few thousand compounds with dense, comparable, same-target measurements delivers congeneric series, MMPs, activity cliffs and a validated QSAR; a million structurally diverse NPs with heterogeneous or absent labels delivers none of those. Depth on a target beats breadth across chemistry for every analysis the platform actually wants to run. Right-sized target: order 10^3-10^4 in-domain compounds, set by curation capacity and by the 771-scaffold coverage floor I measured, NOT by the 1,122,178 records COCONUT will hand you.

(4) MAKE PROVENANCE AND LICENCE FIRST-CLASS SCHEMA, AND MAKE AUDITABILITY THE RATE LIMIT. Tier every record by structure confirmation (X-ray/synthesis > deposited FIDs > computational-NMR-consistent > spectroscopy-only) rather than by boolean "validated", so the documented ~14% misassignment rate becomes a stated bound instead of an invisible contaminant. Partition by licence tier and never merge across tiers in a shipped artifact — ChEMBL's CC BY-SA copyleft, NPAtlas's CC BY-NC, KNApSAcK's explicit prohibition, COCONUT's unresolved CC0-vs-CC-BY conflict, and the licence-SILENT group (NPASS, CMAUP, TCMSP, SymMap, ZINC-22) which is the real legal exposure precisely because it looks open. And impose the discipline that the corpus may only grow as fast as its gates can be validated against a hand-checked gold standard: keep the current 8, expand them to a ~100-compound tier-1 gold set, and make them a permanent regression suite every ingestion run must reproduce.

TWO NUMBERS THAT SHOULD SETTLE THE FRAMING DEBATE INTERNALLY. First: I measured the 8 curated compounds at 12.5% CNS-physicochemically plausible (only Huperzine A passes; Onjisaponin V is MW 1,764 with TPSA 627 and 28 rotatable bonds) versus 27.45% for a random draw from NPAtlas. The hand-picked cognition set scores WORSE than random on the platform's own defining pharmacological gate — that is direct evidence that curation-by-literature-prominence introduced bias, and it is only visible against a background. Second: the 8 compounds have 8 distinct Murcko scaffolds and 0 of 28 pairwise Tanimoto similarities above 0.40, so the set is simultaneously too small for statistics and too diverse for SAR — the worst of both regimes. Expansion is genuinely necessary. Unbounded expansion would trade a small, honest, auditable dataset for a large, unfalsifiable one, and the ultra-large-library literature the proposal would cite in its favour actually says the opposite of what it is usually quoted as saying: Lyu et al. found that library growth improved performance only when the method already discriminated on small benchmarks, and that "when docking performed poorly in small benchmarks, performance often deteriorated with library size." Earn the discrimination at 10^3 with a real background and real negatives; only then does scale pay.

CAVEATS ON MY OWN NUMBERS, stated so they are not over-read: the CNS heuristic (MW<=450, TPSA<=90, HBD<=3, cLogP 1-5, RotB<=8) is my own composite, not a single published rule, and Huperzine A and Ginkgolide B show CNS-active NPs exist outside naive filters; the 27.45% and 11,185-scaffold figures are measured on NPAtlas only (microbial, no plants) and do not generalise to all NP space without re-measurement; the five-gate survival product (0.232) assumes independence which the evidence explicitly contradicts, so treat it as illustrative, not measured; and the ~354 core-hour docking estimate for 1.12M molecules is my linear scaling of Lyu et al.'s 43,563 core hours for 138M, not a benchmark I ran.

## 1. The Inclusion Protocol

### 1.1 The denominator, stated first

> **D(np-cognition-v2)** is the set of chemical records that (a) appear in at least one **Tier-A source release pinned by SHA-256 in the protocol manifest**, and (b) survive hard filters **H1–H9**, after standardization pipeline **S1–S8**.
>
> D is **not** "all natural products". It is not "COCONUT". It is a stated function of a pinned set of files and a versioned predicate. Every rate the platform publishes must name `D(np-cognition-v2)` and its release pins, or it is undefined.

The four candidate denominators differ by an order of magnitude and describe different populations — COCONUT live 1,122,178 / LOTUS 227,319 structures / NPASS 192,587 with structure / ChEMBL flag 98,989 (89% wrong per above). Naming which one you used is not pedantry; it is the difference between a rate and a number.

**Every corpus statistic must ship with the cascade**, in the style of COCONUT 2.0's own (~1.5M imported → 1,022,536 → 695,133; ~54% attrition). The cascade is a first-class artifact, not a log line.

### 1.2 Hard filters (fail any → not in D)

| # | Criterion | Exact threshold | Action | Justification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **H1** | Parses and sanitizes | `Chem.MolFromSmiles(s)` non-None after `rdMolStandardize.Cleanup` | REJECT | Measured 0/1000 loss on ChEMBL; COCONUT 2.0 lost ~32% of raw imports at the ChEMBL-checker valence step, so expect real attrition on bulk sources |
| **H2** | Element whitelist | largest fragment ⊆ {H,B,C,N,O,F,Si,P,S,Cl,Se,Br,I}; any other element → QUARANTINE (not reject — organometallic NPs are real) | QUARANTINE | Keeps vitamin B12-class chemistry visible instead of silently gone |
| **H3** | Single principal component | after `LargestFragmentChooser`, `heavy(largest)/heavy(total) ≥ 0.50` | else QUARANTINE as `MIXTURE` | Salts pass (bromide is 1/17 of neostigmine); true co-crystals and mixtures do not. Catches the two salt records already in `corpus_ACHE.json` |
| **H4** | Size | `6 ≤ heavy_atoms ≤ 150` | REJECT | Lower bound drops solvents/fragments. Upper: Onjisaponin V is 123 HA and is a legitimate NP; 150 keeps it and excludes polymer artifacts |
| **H5** | Mass | `MW ≤ 2000 Da` (unchanged from v1) | REJECT | Onjisaponin V 1,764 Da is the working ceiling case |
| **H6** | **NP evidence** | ≥1 of: (a) record present in LOTUS / NPAtlas / CyanoMetDB / COCONUT / NPASS **with an organism assignment**; (b) `ChEMBL.natural_product=1` **AND** skeleton match to an (a) source. **(b) alone is never sufficient.** | REJECT | This is the H that fixes the 89% error. The ChEMBL flag is a bioactivity join key, never an NP definition |
| **H7** | Provenance floor | ≥1 resolvable source accession (`source`,`release`,`source_record_id`) | REJECT | `provenance.Provenance.__post_init__` already refuses `DATABASE` status without `source_id`; H7 is that rule pushed to the record level |
| **H8** | Licence tier assigned | one of `PUBLIC`,`COPYLEFT`,`NONCOMMERCIAL`,`INTERNAL_ONLY` (§2.3) | REJECT | A record we cannot describe legally cannot be stored in a partition |
| **H9** | Stereo tractability | `implied_stereoisomers = 2^(undef_atoms + undef_bonds) ≤ 64`, i.e. **≤ 6 undefined stereo elements** | else → `quarantine/stereo_unresolved` | See §3.5. Ginsenoside Rg1 (21 undefined → 2.1M isomers) fails and *must* fail |

H9 is a **partition boundary, not a deletion**: `quarantine/stereo_unresolved` records stay on disk, are counted in the cascade, and are available as decoys — they are just barred from every headline count and every 3D output.

### 1.3 Scored preferences (recorded, never exclude)

Each is stored as a `provenance.Value`, not a bare float.

| Field | Range | Status | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cns_mpo_5` | 0–5 (§6 — deliberately **not** 6) | `COMPUTED` | in-domain / out-of-domain partition |
| `stereo_completeness` | `1 − undef/total`, or 1.0 if no centres | `COMPUTED` | tiering, 3D eligibility |
| `structure_confidence_tier` | T1–T4 (§5 G9) | `LITERATURE` (T1–T3) / `DATABASE` (T4) | gates quantitative claims |
| `activity_evidence_tier` | A0–A3 (§7) | varies | gates target claims |
| `n_reference_dois` | int | `DATABASE` | provenance depth |
| `n_independent_documents` | int | `LITERATURE` | de-inflated activity count |
| `interference_flags` | list (§5 G4) | `COMPUTED` | triage, never rejection |
| `source_multiplicity` | int | `COMPUTED` | detects circular re-import; high multiplicity ≠ high confidence |

`source_multiplicity` deserves a note: 40 of 50 open NP databases overlap ≥50% with another, and COCONUT 2.0's authors document errors propagating by mutual re-import. Weighting by record count silently upweights the most-copied compounds — the promiscuous polyphenols. We record multiplicity and **never** use it as a confidence signal.

### 1.4 Protocol object

Extend the existing frozen dataclass rather than replacing it:

```python
# platform/cbc/corpus.py

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InclusionProtocolV2(InclusionProtocol):
    version: str = "np-cognition-v2"
    description: str = (
        "Records from pinned Tier-A natural-product source releases that carry an "
        "organism assignment from a curated NP source, survive RDKit standardization "
        "S1-S8, and have at most 6 undefined stereo elements.")

    # -- hard filters (H1-H9) --
    element_whitelist: tuple[str, ...] = ("H","B","C","N","O","F","Si","P","S",
                                          "Se","Cl","Br","I")
    min_principal_fragment_fraction: float = 0.50   # H3
    min_heavy_atoms: int = 6                        # H4
    max_heavy_atoms: int = 150                      # H4
    max_mol_weight: float = 2000.0                  # H5 (inherited)
    require_np_source_with_organism: bool = True    # H6 -- the fix
    trust_chembl_np_flag_alone: bool = False        # H6 -- measured 89% FP
    max_undefined_stereo_elements: int = 6          # H9 -> 2**6 = 64

    # -- pinned releases: the denominator's actual definition --
    source_pins: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = (
        # (source, release, sha256_of_raw_file)  -- filled by the manifest writer
    )

    def digest(self) -> str:
        """Protocol identity. Any threshold change changes this, and it is written
        onto every compound row, so no result can outlive the protocol that made it."""
        import hashlib, json
        return "prot_" + hashlib.blake2b(
            json.dumps(self.to_dict(), sort_keys=True).encode(), digest_size=8).hexdigest()
```

`digest()` deliberately mirrors `mem._digest`. The protocol JSON is written to `data/corpus/protocol/<digest>.json` and registered in the ledger with `Ledger.artifact()`.

## 3. Standardization pipeline

One function, `platform/cbc/standardize.py::standardize_record`, called by every adapter. Ordering is load-bearing.

### 3.1 The exact RDKit sequence

```python
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize import rdMolStandardize
from rdkit.Chem.inchi import MolToInchiKey

_LFC   = rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser()
_UNCHG = rdMolStandardize.Uncharger()
_TE    = rdMolStandardize.TautomerEnumerator()
_TE.SetMaxTautomers(1000); _TE.SetMaxTransforms(1000)

# S1  parse. On failure re-parse sanitize=False to CLASSIFY the error.
#     chem.validate_smiles already does exactly this -- reuse it, do not reimplement.
mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles)                       # 0.043 ms

# S2  Cleanup = RemoveHs + MetalDisconnector + Normalizer + Reionizer + AssignStereochemistry
mol = rdMolStandardize.Cleanup(mol)                    # ~0.09 ms

# S3  largest fragment -- BUT record what was removed, never silently drop it
frags = Chem.GetMolFrags(mol, asMols=True)
parent = _LFC.choose(mol)                              # 0.023 ms
discarded = [Chem.MolToSmiles(f) for f in frags
             if Chem.MolToSmiles(f) != Chem.MolToSmiles(parent)]
frac = parent.GetNumHeavyAtoms() / max(mol.GetNumHeavyAtoms(), 1)
if frac < 0.50:  raise GateFail("H3_MIXTURE", frac=frac, components=discarded)

# S4  neutralize. Uncharger preserves permanently-charged centres (quaternary N),
#     so neostigmine stays a cation and its InChIKey keeps the -M suffix. Correct.
parent = _UNCHG.uncharge(parent)                       # 0.016 ms

# S5  STEREO PERCEPTION -- before any key, and with FindPotentialStereo not
#     FindMolChiralCenters: 0.014 ms vs 0.685 ms, and it sees bond stereo too.
si = Chem.FindPotentialStereo(parent)                  # 0.014 ms
undef_atoms = sum(1 for e in si if e.type == Chem.StereoType.Atom_Tetrahedral
                  and e.specified != Chem.StereoSpecified.Specified)
undef_bonds = sum(1 for e in si if e.type == Chem.StereoType.Bond_Double
                  and e.specified != Chem.StereoSpecified.Specified)

# S6  KEYS (§3.3)
inchikey  = MolToInchiKey(parent)                      # 0.109 ms  <- PRIMARY KEY
skeleton  = inchikey.split("-")[0]                     #            <- reconciliation index

# S7  TAUTOMER KEY -- computed, NEVER substituted for the record's structure
try:
    taut_key = MolToInchiKey(_TE.Canonicalize(parent)) # 8.4 ms mean, 235 ms worst seen
except Exception:
    taut_key = None; flags.append("TAUT_TIMEOUT")

# S8  descriptors + interference, via the existing chem.validate_smiles report
```

### 3.2 Why tautomer canonicalization does not touch the stored structure

This is the single most consequential choice in the pipeline, so it gets a paragraph.

`TautomerEnumerator.Canonicalize` is used **only** to compute `tautomer_key`, a duplicate-*suspicion* index. The record's `canonical_smiles` remains the standardized parent of what the source actually asserted. Three reasons:

1. **The ledger never merges contradictions.** Curcumin is deposited everywhere as the 1,3-diketone but exists in solution only as the enol tautomers. Overwriting the deposited structure with RDKit's canonical choice destroys the source's assertion and replaces it with ours, silently, at scale. What we can honestly say is "these two records are tautomer-related", and that is what `tautomer_key` says.
2. **40% of tautomeric conflicts involve a change in stereochemistry** (Guasch 2016). Canonicalizing can therefore *reassign stereo* — the exact defect the platform exists to prevent.
3. **Cost.** At 8.4 ms mean it is 77% of the pipeline's per-molecule budget, and 235 ms on a real platform compound (Salvianolic Acid B, 544 tautomers). Making it advisory rather than mandatory means it can be deferred, batched, or skipped for the size tail without changing identity.

Natural products are specifically enriched for the hardest case: ring–chain tautomerism is possible for ~16% of compounds in NP and approved-drug databases.

### 3.3 Primary key: **full standard InChIKey**, not skeleton

**Primary key = full 27-character standard InChIKey of the standardized parent.**

The skeleton (first 14 characters, the connectivity-layer hash) collapses stereochemistry, isotopes, and protonation state. It also collapses *some* tautomers (those inside a standard-InChI mobile-H group) but not others (keto–enol generally survives) — which is precisely why it cannot be an identity and why `tautomer_key` exists separately.

Demonstrated on the platform's own data this session:

```
Huperzine A, isomeric : ZRJBHWIHUMBLCN-YQEJDHNASA-N
Huperzine A, flattened: ZRJBHWIHUMBLCN-UHFFFAOYSA-N     <- same skeleton, different molecule
physostigmine         : PIJVFDBKTWXHHD-HIFRSBDPSA-N
(+)-physostigmine     : PIJVFDBKTWXHHD-AWKYBWMHSA-N     <- enantiomers, different activity
```

Keying on the skeleton would merge (−)- and (+)-physostigmine into one row. They are different drugs. **Stereoisomers of a natural product are different molecules with different activity; the key must not merge them.** v1's `corpus.py` already got this right and documented it — keep it, and keep the reasoning in the docstring.

The skeleton's job is the *reconciliation index* (§4), and it is exactly the right tool there: cross-database agreement rises 15–20 points (max +47.4) when stereo is discarded, meaning most cross-source "disagreement" is stereo. Skeleton-grouping finds those groups; it does not resolve them.

```sql
inchikey     TEXT PRIMARY KEY   -- identity
skeleton     TEXT NOT NULL      -- indexed; reconciliation only
tautomer_key TEXT               -- nullable; suspicion index only
```

### 3.4 What happens to a record with undefined stereocentres

Four states, keyed on `U = undef_atoms + undef_bonds`. This replaces the current behaviour where `validate.py::check_chemistry` fails the whole gate on any undefined centre — correct at n=8, unusable at n=10⁵ where 27.9% of records (measured) would fail.

| State | Condition | In D? | 2D stats | 3D / docking / affinity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `STEREO_DEFINED` | U = 0 | yes | yes | **yes** |
| `STEREO_PARTIAL` | 1 ≤ U ≤ 2 (≤4 isomers) | yes | yes | **enumerate all 2^U, report the ensemble.** Never pick one. Each isomer is a child record with `DERIVES_FROM` and `Status.PREDICTED` |
| `STEREO_AMBIGUOUS` | 3 ≤ U ≤ 6 (≤64 isomers) | yes | yes | **hard-blocked.** All 3D fields emit `provenance.not_computed(note=...)` |
| `STEREO_UNRESOLVED` | U > 6 | **no** (H9) | quarantine partition only | blocked |

The 2 / 6 cut-offs are **engineering thresholds, stated as such**: 4 poses is a reportable ensemble; 64 is the practical ceiling for exhaustive enumeration and honest ranking on a laptop. They are not derived from data and should be labelled that way in the protocol JSON.

The justification for blocking rather than guessing is external: ten Brink & Exner showed GOLD and PLANTS both fail to rank stereoisomers correctly, so a docking score computed on an arbitrarily chosen isomer is noise presented as a measurement. Ginsenoside Rg1's 21 undefined centres → 2^21 ≈ 2.1M implied molecules; the platform already flags this in `validation_report.json`, and H9 turns that flag into a gate.

Existing `chem.SmilesReport.implied_stereoisomers` is exactly the field this consumes. Keep it; extend it to include bond stereo (currently atoms only).

### 3.5 Absent stereo vs asserted flat stereo

`smiles_kind` on `SourceRecord` matters here. A record from a source that only publishes canonical (non-isomeric) SMILES has *unknown* stereo, not *flat* stereo. 24% of LOTUS lacks isomeric SMILES; NPAtlas is 73.7% tetrahedral. Conflating these produces false stereo conflicts in §4. The gate distinguishes `STEREO_ABSENT_IN_SOURCE` from `STEREO_UNDEFINED_IN_STRUCTURE`.

## 4. Deduplication and cross-source reconciliation

**Governing rule, inherited from `mem.py`:** disagreement is a deliverable, not a defect. `memory/views/disputes.md` already says it — *"Never auto-resolved: in a critical-review system the record of disagreement is the deliverable."* The corpus obeys the same rule.

### 4.1 Three-level match, three different meanings

| Level | Key | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 exact | identical `inchikey` **and** identical standardized canonical SMILES | same molecule | **MERGE** — union of source attributions only |
| L2 stereo group | identical `skeleton`, different `inchikey` | either genuine stereoisomers **or** a stereo error | **NEVER MERGE.** Emit a `StereoGroup` |
| L3 tautomer group | identical `tautomer_key`, different `skeleton` | tautomer-related records | **NEVER MERGE.** Emit a `TautomerGroup`, flag for review |

Merge at L1 is strictly additive: append to `source_attribution`, union `organisms`, union `references`, union `activities`. **No scalar is ever overwritten** — descriptors are recomputed from the single canonical structure, so there is nothing to reconcile.

### 4.2 Stereo conflict — the 22% case

Within an L2 group, classify before escalating:

- **SPECIFICATION vs ABSENCE**: one member has U=0 with an isomeric SMILES from a DOI-bearing source (NPAtlas, CyanoMetDB), another has U>0 or `smiles_kind != isomeric`. This is not a contradiction — one source simply says less. Link with `SUPERSEDES` (defined → flat) and keep both rows. Automatable.
- **GENUINE CONFLICT**: ≥2 members with U=0 and *different* assigned configurations, same formula. **Never resolved automatically.** Written to `data/corpus/conflicts/stereo.jsonl` and into the ledger as one `CLAIM` per source assertion (`kind="evidence"`, `source_type="database"`, `source_ref=accession`) plus `RELATES_TO` edges between them. When a human adjudicates, they write a `STATUS` — and `mem.py`'s `v_dispute` view surfaces any target with both VERIFIED and REFUTED records.

Published base rate is 22.1% of unique COCONUT molecules. **Measure our own rate and report it** — that is a corpus health metric, and it is the M2 success criterion (§10).

Note the honest limit: even the COCONUT authors state these "could be different valid stereoisomers of the same base constitution or errors in the databases." Neither we nor they can tell. Recording "we cannot tell, here are both" is the correct output.

### 4.3 Organism disagreement is usually not a disagreement

Organism is **multi-valued and reference-bearing**, stored as rows, not a column:

```sql
CREATE TABLE occurrence (
  inchikey TEXT NOT NULL, taxon_id INTEGER, taxon_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  rank TEXT, reference_doi TEXT, source TEXT NOT NULL, source_release TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (inchikey, taxon_name, reference_doi, source));
```

Two sources naming different organisms for one InChIKey is **normal** — the compound occurs in both. That is an additive union, not a conflict. A conflict exists only when **the same reference DOI is cited as supporting different taxa**; that is a citation error and gets flagged.

`taxon_id` must resolve against NCBI Taxonomy. An unresolvable name is stored (never discarded) but `taxon_id IS NULL`, and **a NULL taxid does not satisfy H6's organism requirement**. The CyanoMetDB `"n.a."` trap and the general name-resolution tail are why.

### 4.4 Activity disagreement: never average, and de-inflate first

Every measurement is a row. Nothing is averaged, ever.

```sql
CREATE TABLE activity (
  inchikey TEXT NOT NULL, target_uniprot TEXT, target_chembl_id TEXT,
  standard_type TEXT, standard_relation TEXT,   -- '=', '>', '<' : keep all three
  standard_value REAL, standard_units TEXT, pchembl_value REAL,
  assay_chembl_id TEXT, document_id TEXT, confidence_score INTEGER,
  article_type TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- PURE_ISOLATE | EXTRACT | UNKNOWN
  source TEXT, source_release TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (inchikey, assay_chembl_id, document_id, standard_type, standard_value));
```

Three de-inflation rules, all forced by measured facts in the evidence:

1. **Re-citation collapse.** 90% of matched pairs in ChEMBL Ki data are repeated citations of a single measurement, not replicates. Report `n_independent_documents = COUNT(DISTINCT document_id)`, **never** `COUNT(*)`. A compound with 40 activity rows from 2 papers has 2 measurements.
2. **NPASS↔ChEMBL overlap.** NPASS v3.0 activity is substantially integrated from ChEMBL v35. Dedupe on `(reference, target, standard_type, round(value, 2))` across sources before counting, or the same measurement is counted twice with two provenance stamps.
3. **Aggregate as median + full range + n, never mean.** True experimental uncertainty on public Ki is mean error 0.44 pKi, SD 0.54; the maximum achievable R² for any model on large public sets is ~0.81. Any aggregation that hides the spread is claiming precision that does not exist. Mixed public IC50 SD is only ~25% larger than Ki SD — assay heterogeneity is a minor problem next to provenance.

Censored rows (`>`, `<`) are **kept and tagged**, not dropped. They are the negatives the corpus has none of, and without negatives ROC AUC, precision, specificity, EF and BEDROC are all *undefined* (denominator zero), not merely noisy.

Implemented as new methods on the existing `validate.Gate` class, so `platform/validate.py` remains the single exit-non-zero gate. Each gate declares **threshold** and **action** ∈ {REJECT, QUARANTINE, FLAG}.

| Gate | Check | Threshold | Action | Measured / expected rate |

| **G1** structure validity | parse + sanitize (reuse `chem.validate_smiles`, which already re-parses with `sanitize=False` to classify the failure) | must pass | REJECT | 0/1000 on ChEMBL; expect % on bulk COCONUT |

| **G3** stereo completeness | `U = undef_atoms + undef_bonds` | U ≤ 6 (H9); tiering at 0 / 2 / 6 | REJECT above 6, else FLAG | 27.9% of molecules carry ≥1 undefined (measured); COCONUT 2.0 residual is 12.0% of stereocentre-bearing records |

Until it is obtained, only the physchem arm runs, and the flag must say which arm fired.** |
| **G5** activity provenance | classify every activity row `PURE_ISOLATE` / `EXTRACT` / `UNKNOWN` | assay description matched against an extract lexicon: *extract, decoction, infusion, fraction, essential oil, crude, tincture, herb, powder, juice, oil of* → EXTRACT. ChEMBL `confidence_score ≥ 8` + defined structure → PURE_ISOLATE. Everything else UNKNOWN | EXTRACT and UNKNOWN excluded from potency aggregation, retained as annotation | ~57% of NAPRALERT activity reports are extract-level. ~22% of pharmacology studies characterise the extract half the time or less |
| **G5b** activity claim floor | a compound may carry "active against T" only with ≥1 `PURE_ISOLATE` row with a pChEMBL value at `confidence_score ≥ 8` | hard | else evidence tier drops to A0 | — |

| **G8** element whitelist | §1.2 H2 | — | QUARANTINE | |
| **G9** structure-confidence tier | T1 X-ray or total synthesis; T2 raw FIDs deposited; T3 computational NMR (DP4+/DU8+) consistent; T4 spectroscopic assignment only | default **T4** | FLAG; only T1–T2 may carry a quantitative claim | **~14% of published NP structures are wrong** (Kutateladze DU8+; Zimmerman predicted 10–22%). >200 misassigned marine NPs 2010–2021 alone. **Automated assignment can reach T4 and sometimes T3. **Why G4 flags and never rejects.** 68% of the 480 PAINS alerts derive from ≤4 compounds each; all 480 came from one proprietary library in six AlphaScreen assays. 97% of PubChem compounds containing a PAINS alert were *infrequent* hitters. 109 alerts occur in Dark Chemical Matter, and 87 FDA-approved drugs contain one. PAINS is a triage prompt, not a classifier. v1's `exclude_pains: bool = False` with its docstring already had this right.

**Gate output contract.** Every gate writes one row to `gate_result(run_id, inchikey|source_record_id, gate, verdict, detail)` and one aggregate `CLAIM` to the ledger. The cascade is `SELECT gate, verdict, count(*) FROM gate_result GROUP BY 1,2` — which is why the cascade is free and cannot drift from the code.

## 6. CNS / BBB relevance filter

### 6.1 What we compute, and what we are honest about not computing

CNS MPO (Wager et al., *ACS Chem Neurosci* 2010, 1:435) sums six desirability functions, each mapped to [0,1]:

| Term | Desirable (=1.0) | Undesirable (=0.0) | Can RDKit do it? |
|---|---|---|---|
| ClogP | ≤ 3 | ≥ 5 | yes (`Crippen.MolLogP`) |
| ClogD₇.₄ | ≤ 2 | ≥ 4 | **no** |
| MW | ≤ 360 | ≥ 500 | yes |
| TPSA | 40–90 (hump: 0 at ≤20 and ≥120) | | yes |
| HBD | ≤ 0.5 | ≥ 3.5 | yes |
| pK*a* (most basic) | ≤ 8 | ≥ 10 | **no** |

RDKit computes four of six. ClogD₇.₄ and most-basic-pK*a* have no reliable free implementation.

**Therefore the platform computes `cns_mpo_4` — a four-term score out of 4.0 — and labels it that. It must never be called "CNS MPO", and the two missing terms are emitted as `provenance.not_computed()`, not silently dropped or substituted.** Substituting ClogP for ClogD (a common shortcut) would produce a number that looks like CNS MPO, scores on the same scale, and is a different quantity. That is exactly the failure mode `provenance.py` was written to prevent.

The published threshold — ≥4 of 6 is "desirable", satisfied by 74% of marketed CNS drugs — **does not transfer to a 4-point scale**. We report the raw `cns_mpo_4` and the per-term breakdown, and set the in-domain partition boundary at `cns_mpo_4 ≥ 3.0` while stating plainly that this cut-off is chosen by us, not published.

`chem.SmilesReport.cns_mpo_flags` already implements the boolean version (MW>360, TPSA>90, HBD>3, cLogP>5). Keep it as the human-readable flag list; add the continuous score alongside.

### 6.2 How weak this is for natural products — stated in the schema, not just the docs

- **Applicability domain violation.** CNS MPO was fit on marketed CNS drugs and Pfizer candidates — synthetic small molecules. Measured against a real NP corpus: **72.55% of 36,453 NPAtlas structures fail a composite CNS gate** (MW≤450, TPSA≤90, HBD≤3, cLogP∈[1,5], RotB≤8). Dominant failures: TPSA>90 (56.7%), MW>450 (41.4%). NP space is systematically enriched for glycosylated, polar, high-MW scaffolds — exactly what the filter excludes.
- **It rejects known CNS-active natural products.** Ginkgolide B (TPSA 149), Asiatic Acid (cLogP 5.03), Curcumin (TPSA 93, 8 RotB) all fail. Of the platform's own 8, only Huperzine A passes — 12.5%, *worse than a random draw from NPAtlas at 27.45%*.
- **Silent on transport.** No efflux (P-gp), no uptake (OATP, LAT1), no carrier-mediated entry. Passive-permeability heuristics on compounds whose real route is transporter-mediated are not weakly predictive; they are off-topic.
- **Silent on metabolism.** Ginsenosides act in vivo substantially via gut-microbiome metabolites (compound K). A parent-structure filter cannot see a molecule that is not the one being tested.
- **Undefined outside small molecules.** For peptides, macrocycles, and anything the platform's `peptide.py` handles, CNS MPO is not weak — it is meaningless. Emit `not_computed`, not a low score. A low score implies it was assessed.

### 6.3 Consequently

1. **Never a hard filter.** It partitions `in_domain` / `out_of_domain`. **Both are retained**, because out-of-domain records are the property-matched decoy pool that enrichment mathematically requires (DUD-E pairs each ligand with 50 property-matched, topologically dissimilar decoys precisely so enrichment measures recognition rather than physicochemical bias).
2. **Measured data always overrides.** If a logBB, brain:plasma ratio, CSF concentration, or curated CNS-drug-list membership exists, it is stored with `Status.MEASURED` + citation and takes precedence. The heuristic is `Status.COMPUTED`; the *inference* "this compound is CNS-penetrant" is `Status.PREDICTED` and carries `applicability="CNS MPO domain is synthetic small molecules; 72.6% of a reference NP corpus falls outside it"`. `provenance.Provenance` has an `applicability` field for exactly this and it should be populated, not left empty.
3. **Report both counts, always.** "N in domain of M total" — never M alone, never N alone.
